Classify nutritional status

Source: R/ref-classify.R
wgh_classify.Rd

With system = "who" (default) the WHO cut-offs are applied: for children under 5 years (WHO 2006 standards) BMI-for-age above 2 SD is overweight and above 3 SD is obesity, and from 5 years (WHO 2007 reference) above 1 SD is overweight and above 2 SD is obesity. Thinness is BMI-for-age below -2 SD (severe below -3 SD) and stunting is height-for-age below -2 SD (severe below -3 SD).

Usage

wgh_classify(x, system = c("who", "cdc"))

Arguments

x

Data with age, height, weight (or existing haz and baz for the WHO system). Z-scores are computed when missing.

system

"who" or "cdc".

Value

x with factor columns height_status and bmi_status, and logical indicators stunting, severe_stunting, thinness, overweight (overweight but not obese), obesity, overweight_obesity and, for the WHO system under 10 years, underweight. With the CDC system the z-scores used are stored in haz_cdc and baz_cdc.

Details

With system = "cdc" the CDC percentile rules for children aged 2 to 20 years are applied to z-scores computed against the CDC 2000 charts: underweight below the 5th BMI percentile, overweight from the 85th to below the 95th percentile and obesity at or above the 95th percentile. Short stature is height below the 3rd percentile.

Next steps

Count and compare with wgh_prevalence(), test trends with wgh_trend_test() or wgh_gee_trend(), and plot with wgh_plot_status_bars() or wgh_plot_prevalence().

Examples

cl <- wgh_classify(growdat)
table(cl$bmi_status, cl$sex)
#>                  
#>                   Male Female
#>   Severe thinness   40     22
#>   Thinness         151    103
#>   Normal          2693   3057
#>   Overweight       952    651
#>   Obesity          789    205
cdc <- wgh_classify(growdat[growdat$age >= 2, ], system = "cdc")
table(cdc$bmi_status, cdc$sex)
#>                 
#>                  Male Female
#>   Underweight     397    300
#>   Healthy weight 2478   2811
#>   Overweight      765    540
#>   Obesity         826    240
